title: BulkBench: quantization fidelity & throughput notes
body:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a working notebook for the BulkBench run that tries to map throughput gains vs quality regressions when we apply different quantization strategies (INT8/AWQ/FP8/GPTQ) across multiple kernels and model variants. Goal is to produce a matrix we can use for routing/policy decisions: which quantized model + kernel to prefer for a given latency SLO and acceptable quality delta.

High-level design of BulkBench: quick notes
- Run large multi-axis sweep (model size, context length, quant format, kernel variant, batch shape).
- Two traffic modes: single-tenant synthetic load (controlled tokens/sec) and mixed-multi-tenant replay (trace from prod, anonymized).
- Evaluation uses two layered metrics: runtime (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory footprint, GPU util) + quality (task-specific accuracy, perplexity where applicable, distributional drift metrics like KL on logits, and targeted prompt-set regression checks).
- We record microprofiles (kernel hop counts, memcpy times, occupancy) via perf hooks + our microprofiler.

Experiment grid (abbrev):
- Models: rwd-7b, rwd-13b, public-13b-v2 (replicated), rwd-70b-lite (subset).
- Contexts: 128, 1024, 4096 tokens.
- Quant modes: fp16 (baseline), int8-awq, int8-gptq, fp8-e4m3 (prototype), per-channel vs per-tensor variants.
- Kernels: kernelA (vector-lane optimized), kernelB (memory-packed), kernelC (fallback generic).
- Batch shapes: (1, 4, 8, 16) for inference concurrent requests; streaming mode + long-run sampling.

Sampling & evaluation prompts
- 3 prompt sets: generic LLM completion (500 short prompts), code reasoning (open-source repo snippets, 200 prompts), QA/closed-book (SQuAD-like, 300), and a tiny hallucination probe (50 antagonistic prompts).
- For each run we capture: top-1 logits, tokens/sec, per-step p95 latency, and per-prompt quality score (exact match / EM or normalized edit distance depending on task).
- Baseline is fp16 kernel with kernelA on the same hardware. All deltas expressed vs baseline.

Preliminary observations (empirical)
1) Throughput vs quality snapshot
- INT8-AWQ on rwd-13b: median token throughput +1.7x vs fp16 when batch >=8 and context <=1024. Quality (QA EM) decline ~1.8 percentage points on average prompts; perplexity increase small (~2.5%).
- INT8-GPTQ produced similar throughput to AWQ but had higher variance on hallucination probe — occasional large deltas on adversarial prompts (single-digit percentage increase in bad answers).
- FP8 prototype sometimes shows throughput gains ~1.3x but quality closer to fp16 (EM delta <0.5%). However, FP8 runs had recurring tail-latency spikes triggered by kernelB memory compaction routines.

2) Kernel behavior and bottlenecks
- kernelA gives best steady-state throughput for small contexts due to lane vectorization, but kernelA is sensitive to attention-kernel quantized weight packing; some int8 packing patterns force extra memcpy and slow warmups (observed 10–20% slow start for first 100 tokens).
- kernelB (memory-packed) performs best for long contexts (4096) but suffers cache-thrashing on mixed workloads causing p99 latency spikes. Root cause appears to be interleaved KV cache allocations with different alignment patterns for int8 vs fp16.
- kernelC consistently has higher latency but better stability under mixed-tenancy — candidate fallback kernel for SLO-preserving rollouts.

3) Mixed workload interference
- When we run replay trace (mix of short/long contexts), quantized kernels sometimes produce transient contention on the PCIe DMA queue due to more frequent memcpy ops per token. This manifests as micro-jitter and p99 tails.
- Observed correlation between memcpy spikes and kernel switching events (runtime switching kernels mid-request when layer shapes hit different vector widths). Need to instrument switch counters and consider sticky-kernel policy.

4) Quality signal nuances
- Aggregate metrics like perplexity mask localized catastrophic regressions. Example: for one code-reasoning prompt set, INT8-AWQ had overall perplexity delta ~+3% but produced 6 prompts with completely incorrect control-flow completions (severity high). So we need per-prompt gating for rollback/alerts, not just average metrics.
- KL on logits against fp16 is a useful quick filter; thresholds tuned at 0.02 KL often catch many bad regressions before they show up in EM. Still misses some adversarial hallucination cases.

Quick numbers (sample) for rwd-13b, context=1024, batch=8 (relative to fp16-kernelA):
- fp16 (baseline): 1200 tokens/sec, p95=110ms, QA-EM=72.3
- int8-awq (kernelA): 2060 tokens/sec (+1.72x), p95=140ms, QA-EM=70.5 (-1.8)
- int8-gptq (kernelA): 1990 tokens/sec (+1.66x), p95=150ms, QA-EM=69.9 (-2.4)
- fp8 (kernelB): 1580 tokens/sec (+1.32x), p95=200ms (spikes), QA-EM=71.8 (-0.5)

Actionable recommendations (short-term)
- Add sticky-kernel policy flag: avoid kernel switch mid-request unless strictly needed. Instrument counter. (ENG-5423)
- Add per-prompt regression hooks: KL threshold check + EM smoke test on critical prompt sets; failover to fp16 if threshold exceeded.
- For AWQ/INT8, add warmup microbatches on cold-start paths to mitigate initial memcpy overhead (small trick: schedule one small dummy request to populate packing).
- For FP8, address kernelB memory compaction routine; propose re-layout of KV cache allocation to reduce alignment mismatches. Nice candidate for profiling PR #3145.

Open questions / longer-term work
- Can kernel selection be traffic-aware? (route long-context to kernelB but reserve kernelC as safety lane)
- How do quantization-aware routing policies interact with Dedicated instances that have pinned GPU topologies?
- Can we build a light-weight on-request online KL estimator to decide on-the-fly whether to serve quantized or fallback fp16?

Next runs planned
- Repeat key points with rwd-70b-lite stripped checkpoint (May 27) focusing on long context (4096) and FP8 variants.
- Isolated memcpy profile with nvprof + microprofiler on kernel switch boundary (May 22) — aim to capture DMA queue saturation traces.
- Run longer-duration mixed-tenant replay for 24 hours to capture low-frequency regression modes (schedule: Jun 2).

Notes / misc
- Data & artifacts: bench CSVs stored under gdrive: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/bulkbench-outputs/may2025/ (will push after next run).
- Quick win: set default rollout for int8-awq to canary 5% on low-risk routes (short completion tasks) with immediate rollback on KL>0.02 or EM delta >2 points.

If you're reviewing: please add experiment IDs for any runs you kick off (use tag bulk-<date>-<id>) and paste run links here. Packets of CSVs are large; prefer storing compressed parquet in bench bucket and referencing the path in Confluence page CONF-6721.

-- Aisha
